key_insight: In multimodal diffusion transformers, image-to-text feedback does not always correct mistakes—it can also preserve them. The paper shows that the evolving image can feed back into text representations in ways that lock in both correct content and errors, and that transplanting these feedback messages can either rescue or ruin generations.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the unclear role of image-to-text feedback in MMDiTs: whether it helps the model recover from prompt deviations or unintentionally reinforces them during image generation.
method: Analyze the joint attention mechanism in MMDiTs to study how evolving image features update internal text representations.
Examine image-to-text feedback as a communication pathway that preserves objects and attributes already present in the image state.
Transplant image-to-text messages between generation runs to test whether the feedback can correct failures or propagate errors.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work reveals a previously underappreciated source of generation bias in multimodal diffusion models. Understanding and controlling image-to-text feedback could improve prompt adherence, reduce error reinforcement, and enable more reliable image synthesis.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing text prompt -> joint attention -> evolving image -> image-to-text feedback -> next-step image update

paper_title: Images Talk Back: Guiding MMDiTs by Suppressing Image-to-Text Feedback
paper_authors: Yucheng Yang, Xiaoxiao Sun, Shusheng Yang, Jiakang Chen, Serena Yeung-Levy
